subject: Recap & Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity plan and SLO inputs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@orbithealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity plan and SLO inputs

Elena / team —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we can move to a scoped Reserved Capacity proposal. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain / drivers you shared:
- Inference latency spikes during nightly batch ingest and morning peak (7–10am PT) causing timeouts for downstream monitoring.
- Data isolation requirement: PHI-containing payloads must remain on dedicated hardware in your VPC.
- Predictable cost and throughput for CA-regulated deployments — need capacity guarantees and support SLA.

Goals you want to achieve with Dedicated: 
1) Stable 99th percentile tail latency below 250ms for 1k rps bursts, with autoscale for sustained peak.
2) Isolation: single-tenant GPU pools in us-west-2 with customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
3) Rolling upgrades with canary traffic and no more than 5 minutes of degraded throughput during model swaps.

Sizing notes we discussed (estimates until we get telemetry):
- Baseline: 8 A100-style GPUs reserved for steady-state (predictable throughput for synchronous endpoints).
- Burst policy: additional 4 GPU burst pool available up to 3x/day for 30–90 minutes (configurable).
- Warm KV cache preference to reduce cold-start latency for long-context models.

Next steps I proposed:
- I will share a draft Reserved Capacity spreadsheet (attached) with pricing tiers and SLO targets.
- You to confirm: expected sustained RPS during peak window and any planned model size changes (we assumed a 13B/30B family for the baseline).
- Security: procurement to send any additional SOC2/infra questions; we can attach our SOC2 packet and network diagrams.

Attachments: orbit_dedicated_capacity_draft.xlsx (pricing + sizing), slo-summary-20260501.pdf (SLO options).

If that looks right, I’ll schedule a follow-up demo with Marcus (runtime lead) next week to walk through the isolation options and autoscale behaviors.

Thanks —

Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(priyom@redwood.com)
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

---
Note: Draft assumes no on-prem hardware; if OrbitHealth wants on-prem or air-gapped, we’ll convert to Private deployment pricing and add validation steps.
From: Elena Torres <elena@orbithealth.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orbithealth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity plan and SLO inputs

Thanks Priyom — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Peak numbers: our engineering telemetry shows sustained morning peak of ~700 rps for synchronous inference (90s window) and nightly batch windows that briefly spike to ~1.8k rps for short bursts (10–20m). We’ll export a CSV for Marcus.
2) Model roadmap: moving from a 13B baseline to testing a 30B variant in Q3 — please include the cost delta for that option.
3) Isolation: must be single-tenant with customer-managed VPC peering and KMS; SOC2 and network diagrams would be appreciated.
4) SLA ask: can you confirm an SLA with credits for sustained p99 > 300ms? If not, what fallbacks do you recommend?

We’ve attached our procurement intake form to this thread (separate mail) — procurement will take over the contract items, but I wanted to ensure product/ops alignment first.

Happy to proceed with the follow-up demo. Thursday next week is best for Marcus’ team.

Best,
Elena
Head of ML Ops | OrbitHealth AI
elena@orbithealth.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap & Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity plan and SLO inputs

Forwarding Elena’s clarifications — tagging Marcus for sizing/ops input before we send formal proposal.

Marcus — quick questions for the follow-up demo: 
- For the 700 rps sustained plus 1.8k short bursts, do you agree with the 8 + 4 burst GPUs we sketched? If not, what change would you recommend to hit p99 < 250ms for the 13B model and p99 < 350ms for a 30B test?
- Can we guarantee a KMS integration path and outline the network diagram for single-tenant VPC peering (to attach to the SOC2 packet)?

I’ll sync with procurement about the DocuSign and send the HubSpot deal link.

-Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena@orbithealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity plan and SLO inputs

On Sat, May 2, 2026 at 09:04 Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Elena’s clarifications — tagging Marcus for sizing/ops input before we send formal proposal.

Thanks — quick technical reply so procurement and product have concrete options for the proposal: 

Sizing recommendation (conservative):
- Reserve 10 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state to cover sustained 700 rps at 13B with warm cache, targeting p99 ~220–240ms.
- Provision a burst pool of 6 GPUs for short 1.8k bursts (we’ll autoscale into the burst pool using queue-based throttles).
- If OrbitHealth wants to test a 30B model in Q3, we recommend a parallel reserved pool of 4 GPUs for canary traffic and an optional scale-path to convert 4 steady GPUs into 8 via instance replacement; include cold-warm cache warmup windows in the runbook.

Isolation & network: we can do single-tenant GPU pools in us-west-2 with VPC peering and customer-managed routing. KMS integration supported via customer KMS key with HSM-backed encryption — we’ll include the network diagram and key rotation notes in the SOC2 bundle.

SLOs and fallbacks:
- Target SLO: p99 <= 250ms for synchronous endpoints (13B).
- If p99 exceeds 300ms for more than 4% of 30-day windows, we recommend an automatic fallback to a lower-latency 13B variant or a multi-model routing policy.
- SLA: we can offer credits tied to sustained p99 > 350ms for more than 72 continuous hours; details to be finalized with legal/procurement but we can include a draft in the proposal.

I’ll join the demo and bring a short runbook that shows autoscale triggers, cache pre-warming, and model swap steps.

-Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
Attachment: slo-summary-20260501.pdf
